subject.title: feat(tui): opt-in persistence and agent visibility for `!`/`!!` local shell commands

question: Should OpenClaw permanently define TUI `!` as agent-visible after explicit per-session consent and `!!` as persisted history-only?
rationale: The patch creates a new shell-sharing UX convention and privileged transcript-injection surface; tests can prove mechanics but cannot authorize that permanent product and sensitive-data boundary.

options.title: Approve opt-in sharing
options.body: Adopt the proposed per-session consent model and `!`/`!!` meanings after the truncation fix and missing real-path proof.

options.title: Keep output local-only
options.body: Decline transcript persistence and model visibility while retaining the existing local shell execution behavior.

options.title: Choose another explicit action
options.body: Redesign sharing as a separate command or interaction rather than assigning new semantics to `!` and `!!`.

recommendation.title: Approve opt-in sharing
recommendation.body: Adopt the proposed per-session consent model and `!`/`!!` meanings after the truncation fix and missing real-path proof.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent history spans the TUI shell, session lifecycle, gateway chat, and protocol areas, making this the best available owner for the cross-surface product choice.
